I'll brute force: generate random routes, compute R; retry with different random seeds until R == 64. Each route adds 1 or 2 boundaries; R = 1 + (number of distinct value-change boundaries). With hops chosen distinct, each route adds 2 boundaries. To hit exactly 64: use 31 routes with distinct hops (R=63) + one route where the hop equals the default 0 in a way that creates 1 boundary: e.g. a route [p, p+2^k) with hop 0 → no new boundary (hop same as surrounding 0) ✗; or a /128 route with hop X where the left neighbor run already has hop X: e.g. place a route at position p with hop h equal to the hop of the run containing [p-1,p)... but that run is 0 (default) unless p-1 is another /128 route.

So 31 /128 routes (not in the top half) + 8000::/1 with a distinct hop → R = 1+62+1 = 64 ✓ (assuming the /128 routes are all below 0x8000...). Then a second version.
